note: Resolutions for rail-audit findings. A pileup absent from `resolved` is UNRESOLVED. A pileup is AMBIGUOUS, not invalid -- q=0 is also the correct reading for a genuinely Poisson process. Record WHY. Do not bulk-mark to clear the check.

reasons.ARS.rep_med@0.85 (43.9% pooled): KNOWN DEFECT, RECOMPUTED for the three file-backed substrates (R-173/R-175/R-176). This is the clip's UPPER rail: when R2 == 0 the integrand is 1.0 across the mask, so the integral returns the MASK WIDTH. It was invisible to every prior audit because those counted only the LOWER rail (exactly 0). THE AUDIT FOUND IT WITH NO PRIOR KNOWLEDGE OF THE VALUE, which is the whole argument for pileup-detection over a bounds checklist. Per-substrate, and this is why the breakdown is mandatory: kuramoto rails HIGH (55.9% at 0.85) while pvc-11 (79.2%) and allen-np (70.8%) rail LOW at 0.0 -- opposite directions, which a pooled average cancels. Repaired values in coordinates/{kuramoto,pvc-11,allen-np}.repaired.jsonl.
reasons.I.8_brody_q@6.6107e-05 (72.5% pooled): KNOWN DEFECT, OPEN. The fitter's bounds=(0,1) are a MODEL ASSERTION that the substrate lies between Poisson and GOE (R-144); clustering (q<0) and GUE/GSE (q~1.5/2) are unrepresentable. NOTE the rail sits at 6.6107e-05, NOT at 0.0 -- an optimiser floor, so a bounds checklist testing `== 0.0` would have MISSED it. ⚠ AND THE PER-SUBSTRATE NUMBERS ARE DECISION-RELEVANT FOR TIER B: allen-hpf-cell 100.0%, buzsaki-port-cell 99.4%, pvc-11 99.4%, dr-port-cell 98.6%, lambda-star-classes 100%, qpo-maryland 100%. Those coordinates are not degraded, they are ENTIRELY RAIL -- recomputing them is the difference between data and no data, not a refinement. Repaired fitter I8_brody_q_unbounded exists and is fixtured; the 19,619 Tier B values are unrecomputed.
reasons.I.9_berry_robnik_rho@0.9985 (1.4% pileup: DEFINITIONAL, not a defect. rho is a GOE FRACTION, so [0,1] is correct and no repair can open it -- that is R-148's rail finding and the reason validate_fitters' exp_rho row is left deliberately failing. Caught by signature B (bound-proximity), NOT by exact ties: the values crowd NEAR the bounds without landing on them (poisson 0.0015, clustered 0.0045, goe 0.9965, gue 0.9975), which is exactly the shape a pileup test alone would miss. The axis identifies only in the interior; that is a stated limitation, not a bug.
reasons.III.1_p2 / p3 / p5 / p7 / III.4_scalar_s: UNRESOLVED -- NEW, and the mechanism is NOT identified. Pileups at 0, 1/2000, 0, 1/2400 and 11/12000. I tested the obvious hypothesis (a count/N discreteness floor) and it does NOT cleanly hold: the pileup values are ROUND fractions while the smallest nonzero values have VARYING denominators (1/2922, 1/2908, 1/2892 ...), so these are not simply 1/n for each cell's own n. Every instance is kuramoto and at the LOW end of the axis. Recorded with the evidence and left open rather than guessed at; a resolution needs the p-adic axis definition read, not more counting.
